column1: # experiment: E16 forward attention with FKL: the tensor-core DPP and the SIMT DPP against their unfused alternatives

column9: bf16 output; inputs: the file e16_input_d<D>_s<S>_bh<BH>.bin of E16_INPUT_DIR
column10: generated on the host (written by whichever FKL program runs first
column11: read by pytorch-attention/e16_baselines.py; the size and SHA-256 of every file are at the end of these notes); time_ms_* = per call
column12: from `blocks` blocks of `calls_per_block` calls enqueued back to back between two CUDA events (the GPU time of the call
column13: no host gap between calls; the block lasts about E16_BLOCK_MS)
column14: after a warm-up of at least E16_WARMUP_MS of GPU time; every call launches its own argument set (the operations of the call)
column15: rebuilt before the events; prep_us_per_call = host time (steady_clock) of building that set and releasing the one it replaces
column16: per call; position = place of the variant in the order of its configuration (ORDER: groups rotated by configuration + E16_ROTATE
column17: pair members swapped on odd shifts
column18: SIMT last); t_start_ms and t_end_ms = wall clock of the blocks
column19: for the join with the SM clock sampler; single_ms_median = median of `blocks` single calls
column20: each between two events and synchronised (launch latency included); TFLOP/s = 4 BH S^2 D (halved for causal) / time_ms_median; error against an fp32 attention of the same (dequantised) inputs for the first and the last head; kernels and per-kernel facts from capturing one call into a CUDA graph; the library chooses the tiles (no tuning: <D
column25: 4> are the library's defaults); mma_epilogue_*: o * 1.25 + 0.5; SCHEDULES (columns schedule
column29: split_kv: from the template arguments of the attention kernel; the LDGSTS count of every instantiation is in e16_sass_counts.csv): mma_raw
column30: mma_epilogue_* and the bf16 buffers of the *_unfused variants run the library's bf16 cp.async schedule (16-byte cp.async copies of K and V tiles); the fused int8 and fp8 variants run the library's quantised schedule: the raw quantised bytes are copied with cp.async (8 bytes) into a staging area of shared memory and dequantised shared memory to shared memory inside the kernel
column31: the per-token scales are read from global memory; each path has its own tile sizes (the library's choice). A fused-against-unfused prologue pair therefore compares an in-kernel shared-memory dequantisation pass (half the global bytes for K and V) with a separate dequantisation kernel that writes bf16 to global memory
column32: and the two kernels differ in schedule details and tile sizes as well as in fusion: it is not a pure fusion effect.
